title: Officers and employees
summary: An officer exercises significant authority under federal law; an employee is a lesser functionary whose position does not carry the constitutional office status at issue.
notes:
Buckley connects officer status with significant administration and enforcement of public law. Freytag emphasizes an office established by law and substantial adjudicative duties, including discretion over testimony, evidence, and discovery; Lucia applies the comparison to SEC administrative law judges. A continuing legally defined role and the actual authority it carries are therefore central inquiries.

The exact border remains unsettled in the assigned account. The note contrasts a broader originalist proposal covering ongoing statutory duties with the Court’s significant-authority approach, and points out historical complications involving deputies and apparently ministerial officials. Congress’s label for a position alone does not answer the constitutional question.
